name: Kent A. Kiehl
title: Executive Science Officer and Director of Mobile Imaging, Mind Research Network · Professor of Psychology, Neurosciences and Law, University of New Mexico
bio: Kent Kiehl uses brain imaging to study psychopathy and related conditions, including psychotic disorders, traumatic brain injury, substance use and paraphilias. He designed the Mind Mobile MRI System, which takes the scanner into prisons and other facilities and has produced the largest forensic neuroscience repository in the world.

He received his B.Sc. from the University of California, Davis (1993) and his M.A. (1996) and Ph.D. (2000) from the University of British Columbia, where he trained with Robert Hare and Peter Liddle. He was on the faculty at Yale University and directed the Clinical Cognitive Neuroscience Laboratory at the Institute of Living from 2001 to 2007, when he moved to the Mind Research Network and the University of New Mexico.

He is the author of The Psychopath Whisperer (Crown, 2014), co-editor of the Handbook on Psychopathy and Law (Oxford, 2013), and the 2026 recipient of the Robert D. Hare Lifetime Achievement Award from the Society for the Scientific Study of Psychopathy.
